doc.title: Randy Brecker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 12, 2022

chapter: Michael, influences and the Brecker Brothers
title: Will Lee and the band of brothers
summary: Will Lee's bass parts on 'Sponge'; the band shared ideas, leading to the second record being more collective.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Well the tail end of that piece I played, I don’t know if you could hear it that well that Will Lee is doing this incredible, you know, sixteenth note thing and I’m wondering if you wrote that or did you just give him chords and let him go?
That one I’d have to really hear it. If it was towards the end he probably invented — I was pretty specific, I’ll say that, with a lot of bass parts. But it sounds like he probably just ran with it.

And we were a great band. You know if somebody came up with something we’d put it in right away. For instance there’s a tune called “Sponge” on the first record. And part of that [scats] was mine but that whole section where there’s [scats] a lot of that was Will. Maybe I thought of the changes but the [scats] that was probably Will’s. And we were very close. It was really a band of brothers and it got to the point, which was part of the point of the second record which was called The Brecker Brothers Band where it wasn’t just my writing. Because these guys were first call guys and they all had ideas so we really tried to make it more of a band and it made it a lot easier on me too so I didn’t have to come up with all the music.
